name: ldgsts_loaded
fields: l1.ldgsts_fill_bytes_per_cycle (per-SM LDGSTS fill delivery cap, cluster-local, if below the L2 port)
question: hp cp.async GEMMs (cutlass_dense_cpasync 0.57-0.60, triton_matmul bf16/fp8/fp16 0.50-0.70) are single-cluster 0.83-0.90 but full-gpu 0.5-0.6; HW and sim both charge ~50 % of the time to the DEPBAR / BAR.SYNC wait on cp.async data, the sim just finishes in half the time. The sim's LDGSTS sectors flow through the per-SM L2 port at l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle (122 / 125) and the aggregate l2_read_bytes_per_ns. What is the LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.128 fill delivery of one SM alone (W warps each keeping a 2 KB group in flight), of N SMs at once, and the group completion latency?
probe: tools/microbench/ldgsts_loaded/probe/ldgsts_loaded.cu (see header): N CTAs x W warps, v2: each warp keeps 4 groups (4 x 2 KB slots) in flight: per round issue 4 x cp.async.cg 16 B per lane (2 KB), commit_group, wait_group 3 (retires the oldest), latency = retirement clock - that group's issue clock; 4096 rounds; 24 MiB hot buffer, per-CTA region, discarded warm launch; cells N in {1,16,64,128,SMs} x W in {1,2,4,8}, 8 repetitions, two runs. SASS gate: LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.128 present.
derivation: tools/microbench/ldgsts_loaded/model.py: per cell per-CTA bytes/cycle median, aggregate B/ns median, latency p50/p90. (1) per-SM cap = per-CTA bytes/cycle at N = 1, W = 8 (saturated if W = 4 within 5 %). (2) aggregate at N = SMs, W = 8. (3) N = 1, W = 1 latency vs storage.ldgsts.completion copies_per_group = 4 leaf (h100 430, b300 412) within 20 %, else stop and report.
acceptance: per cell spread (P90 - P10) / median < 10 % for N >= 16; runs agree within 5 % on aggregate; (3) passes.

engine_rules_declared_before_data.A: if the N = 1 saturated per-CTA rate < 0.9 x l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle: field memory_level l1.ldgsts_fill_bytes_per_cycle (cluster-local); MemoryHierarchy::load for async_copy (LDGSTS) requests occupies the per-SM L2 port and DRAM port at that rate instead of l2 / dram.sector_bytes_per_cycle (same flag plumbing as the TMA rate, separate field). Otherwise no leaf.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.B: if the N = SMs aggregate < 0.9 x l2_read_bytes_per_ns while the per-SM cap does not already bind (aggregate < N x per-SM cap x clock): report; no leaf from this protocol.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.gate: full-gpu 500x2 vs full-r7, single cluster vs sc-r7 (cp.async kernels will move; sc MAPE is the gate).

not_allowed: no case tuning; cells, derivation and rule A fixed above; a device failing acceptance gets no leaf.

addenda.text: (reading) v1 waited every group (one group in flight per warp) and is latency-bound: per-CTA bytes/cycle is linear in W (5.5 / 10.8 / 21.4 / 42 at W = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 on both devices, group latency 330-360 flat), so the per-SM cap is only bounded below (>= 42 B/cycle) and rule A cannot be read; the h100 aggregate saturates at 7.4 TB/s (= installed l2_read_bytes_per_ns), b300 reaches 11.6 TB/s latency-bound. Unloaded 2 KB group latency 330 / 344 vs the storage.ldgsts.completion copies_per_group = 4 leaf 430 / 412 (0.77 / 0.84; h100 fails the 20 % check -> reported, nothing installed). v2: 4 groups in flight per warp (wait_group 3); same cells, derivation, rules.

addenda.name: shared_read
addenda.text: Why: on H100 the simulated triton matmul / cutlass sparse / cp.async kernels merge half to two thirds of their L2 reads (simulated L2 read sectors per sector delivered 0.32-0.51) while hardware counters of the same launches give 0.81-0.95 (fg-gemm/merge-hwmet); in the simulation 61-92 percent of consecutive requests to one sector from different CTAs fall inside the installed 240-cycle l2_merge window (fg-gemm/jr21/sector-gaps). The installed window and requests-per-read come from aligned TMA streams. Question: do cp.async (LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.128) requests of different SMs to the same sectors merge at all. Probe change: --group G makes the G consecutive CTAs of a slice read the same region from the same start after the common arrival barrier (lockstep), --rot 1 starts member m chunks / G later (same region, different lines at any time); G = 1 is the old probe. Cells (run_share.sh): all SMs, 4 warps, G = 1, and G in {2, 4} x rot {0, 1}, each under ncu --cache-control none (region L2-resident after the discarded launch) and all (flushed before every launch, fills in flight), two runs, 2 retained launches per cell. r = lts__t_sectors_op_read.sum / l1tex__m_xbar2l1tex_read_sectors.sum per launch of k_ldgsts_loaded. Predictions: if LDGSTS merges like the installed TMA rule, lockstep r is about 1 / G (0.5 and 0.25-0.35) and rot r about 1; if it does not merge, every cell has r >= 0.9. Controls: G = 1 and both rot cells must give r within 0.9..1.1, else the counters do not mean what is assumed and nothing is concluded. Use: lockstep r >= 0.9 in both cache states on a device supports excluding async-copy requests from l2_merge on that device; r <= 0.6 keeps the rule and moves the question to request phase; anything between is reported without a rule. No value is fitted from this.

addenda.name: shared_read_result
addenda.written: after the shared_read data (fg-gemm/ldgsts-share/{h100,b300}; H100 GPU-a8e8506a, B300 GPU-2d2e120b; 20 cells per device, three launches per cell, runs a / b agree)
addenda.text: Controls hold on both devices: G = 1 r 1.000-1.003, rotated cells 0.94-0.99. Lockstep r, both cache states: b300 G = 2 0.50-0.51, G = 4 0.47-0.49 (G = 1 aggregate 18.2 TB/s, below the installed 20.1 TB/s L2 read rate); h100 G = 2 0.66-0.67, G = 4 0.67-0.68 (G = 1 aggregate 7.5 TB/s = the installed L2 read rate, i.e. saturated; lockstep delivers 10.4-10.6 TB/s with about 7.0 TB/s read at the slices). By the declared reading b300 keeps the rule (cp.async requests do merge) and h100 falls in the unassigned band; the strong form 'cp.async never merges' is rejected on both. Read after data, not a declared outcome: r(4) is not below r(2) on either device, i.e. at most about two cp.async requests share one read here (the installed requests-per-read, 4 on h100 and 3 on b300, come from aligned TMA streams); and the saturated device merges less than the unsaturated one. Both readings need cells below the aggregate rate (next addendum). H100 build note: the image's cuobjdump cannot disassemble the cubin, so the SASS count came from cuobjdump -xelf + nvdisasm through a wrapper (artifact tools/ldgsts-h100-shim); five earlier attempts are kept as h100.failed-1..5.

addenda.name: shared_read_unsaturated
addenda.text: Question: below the aggregate L2 read rate, how many cp.async requests share one read, and within what start offset. Probe change: --shift D makes member m of a group start m x D SM cycles after the arrival barrier (clock64 spin). Cells (run_share2.sh, ncu --cache-control none, two runs): CTAS in {16, 32}, 4 warps, lockstep G in {1, 2, 4, 8} and G = 2 rotated; CTAS 32: G = 2 with D in {32, 64, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 1024, 2048}, G = 4 with D in {128, 512}, and 1 warp G in {2, 4}. r as before. Validity: G = 1 and rotated cells within 0.9..1.1; a cell counts as unsaturated when its delivered aggregate is below 70 percent of the device's installed L2 read rate. Derivations fixed here, same forms as l2_merge protocol v1: requests per read N* = argmin over N in {1..8} of the mean over lockstep G of |r(G) - max(1/G, 1/N)|, from unsaturated cells only; merged fraction m(D) = clamp(2 (1 - r(D)), 0, 1) and window = the D where m crosses 0.5 by linear interpolation. Use: if N* and the window agree between runs (N* equal, window within 10 percent) they are candidates for cp.async-specific fields of memory.l2_merge on that device (evidence experimental); if the window is not crossed inside 2048 or the controls fail, nothing is installed. The saturated full-SM result is not used for values.

addenda.name: shared_read_unsaturated_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-gemm/ldgsts-share2/{b300,h100}; B300 GPU-69800327, H100 GPU-ebc96a9f; 23 cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell; reader fg-gemm/ldgsts-share2/read_share.py)
addenda.text: Controls hold (G = 1 r 1.000-1.018, rotated 0.97-1.02); every cell is unsaturated (32 CTAs deliver 24 percent of the installed L2 read rate on b300, 41 percent on h100). b300: lockstep r(G) 0.51-0.52 / 0.505-0.509 / 0.47 at G = 2 / 4 / 8, N* = 2 in both runs (mean error 0.017; 0.11 for N = 3); merged fraction m(D) 0.93-0.97 up to D = 64, 0.92 at 128-256, 0.87-0.92 at 384-512, 0.72-0.73 at 1024, 0.38-0.41 at 2048; window 1756 / 1700 cycles (runs differ by 3.3 percent). By the declared use N = 2 and a window near 1728 are candidates for cp.async fields on b300. h100: lockstep r 0.74-0.78 / 0.68-0.73 / 0.53-0.68 at G = 2 / 4 / 8 (1 warp: 0.665 at G = 2, 0.482 at G = 4), N* fit poor (mean error 0.19); r is 0.72-0.77 at every D from 0 to 2048, m(D) stays at 0.5 and never falls: the window is not crossed, nothing is installable on h100. Reading after data: on neither device does a cp.async follower behave like the installed time window (145 / 240 cycles from aligned TMA streams): b300 keeps merging for one to two thousand cycles, h100 shows no dependence on the start offset at all while the rotated cells (about ten thousand cycles apart on the same region) do not merge. The b300 candidates are therefore not installed yet either: what decides the saving may be which SMs form a group rather than when they ask (next addendum).

addenda.name: shared_read_placement
addenda.text: Question: does the saving of shared cp.async reads depend on which SMs share. Probe change: --far 1 forms a group from the CTAs CTAS / G apart in block index (slice = block index mod CTAS / G) instead of G consecutive ones; the JSON line carries the SM id of every CTA. Cells (run_share3.sh): CTAS in {32, 64, all SMs} x warps {1, 4} x G in {1, 2, 4} x far {0, 1} (G = 1 once), lockstep, cache-control none, two runs. r as before; per cell the SM ids of the members of each group are reported (same SM pair parity, distance in SM id). Readings fixed here: (a) placement decides: far r >= 0.9 where the consecutive cell of the same CTAS / warps / G has r <= 0.8, on both runs; (b) placement does not matter: far and consecutive r within 0.05 of each other in every cell; anything else is reported as mixed. If (a): the engine's merge may only join requests of SMs of one group and the group has to be measured (which SM ids pair) before any rule; real kernels whose sharers are spread over the SMs would then merge little, as the hardware counters of the triton matmul and cp.async GEMM launches show. If (b): the difference between probe and kernels lies elsewhere and no rule follows from this run.

addenda.name: shared_read_placement_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-gemm/ldgsts-share3/{h100,b300}; H100 GPU-ebc96a9f, B300 GPU-69800327; 30 cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell)
addenda.text: Reading (a) holds on both devices and both runs: groups of CTAs far apart in block index give r 0.96-1.06 on h100 and 0.88-0.99 on b300, the consecutive groups of the same CTAS / warps / G give 0.29-0.78 and 0.30-0.53. The recorded SM ids show why: consecutive CTAs are dispatched to neighbouring SMs (with all SMs every pair is SM 2k and 2k + 1), the far groups hold SMs at least six ids apart. All SMs, one warp: pairs r 0.51, groups of four consecutive SMs r 0.29-0.31. So shared cp.async reads are saved only between neighbouring SMs; on h100 the start offset does not matter (previous addendum), and kernels whose sharers are spread over the SMs save about a tenth of their reads (hardware counters, fg-gemm/merge-hwmet). The installed requests-per-read of l2_merge (4 on h100, 3 on b300, from groups of consecutive CTAs) is then a property of the neighbourhood, not a count of requests. Which SM ids form one neighbourhood is measured next.

addenda.name: shared_read_domain
addenda.text: Question: which SMs save each other's cp.async reads. Probe change: --smid-mask M makes every SM read the region indexed by (its SM id with the M bits cleared), so SMs whose ids differ only inside M read the same lines in lockstep; all SMs run one CTA. Cells (run_share4.sh): all SMs, warps in {1, 4}, M in {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64} (M = 0 is the disjoint control, the single bits pair SM s with s xor M) and M in {3, 6, 7, 15, 31, 63, 127, 255} (groups of ids sharing the upper bits), two runs. r as before. Derivation fixed here, from the one-warp cells: a single bit b belongs to the domain if r(M = b) <= 0.6 and is outside if r >= 0.9 (between: unassigned); the domain is the set of SM ids equal after clearing the domain bits, accepted only if (i) its bits are contiguous from bit 0 (domain = floor(id / S) with S a power of two), (ii) r(M = S - 1) is within 0.1 of 1 / S, and (iii) r(M = 2S - 1) is within 0.1 of r(M = S - 1) (a larger group saves nothing more); runs must agree on the bit set. If accepted, the engine rule is: an L2 read may be shared only by requests of SMs of one domain; the installed window and requests-per-read stay as measured for requests inside a domain. If the bits are not contiguous or a check fails, the result is recorded and no rule is installed from it. The four-warp cells are reported only. The same question for TMA tile loads is not answered by this probe; the engine rule would rest on the l2_merge v1 cells having used consecutive CTAs as well, which is stated as an assumption until measured.

addenda.name: shared_read_domain_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-gemm/ldgsts-share4/{h100,b300}; H100 GPU-25471ff1, B300 GPU-af5437c6; 32 cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell; every SM id 0..131 / 0..147 present)
addenda.text: One warp, r of run a / run b. Single bits, h100 | b300: M = 1 0.504 / 0.504 | 0.511 / 0.517 (inside); M = 2 0.976 | 1.000, M = 4 1.007 | 1.000, M = 8 1.007 | 1.000 (outside); M = 16 0.780 / 0.778 | 0.797 / 0.793, M = 32 0.753 / 0.738 | 0.797 / 0.803, M = 64 1.009 | 0.892 (unassigned). Groups: M = 3 0.497 | 0.511, M = 7 0.495 | 0.511-0.517, M = 15 0.46 | 0.49, M = 31 0.33-0.35 | 0.33-0.34, M = 63 0.33 | 0.29-0.30, M = 127 0.31 | 0.28, M = 255 0.31 | 0.275. Declared derivation: the domain bits are {bit 0} on both devices and both runs, contiguous from bit 0, S = 2; check (ii) r(M = 1) is within 0.02 of 1 / 2; check (iii) r(M = 3) is within 0.01 of r(M = 1). Accepted: the sharing domain is floor(SM id / 2), i.e. the SMs 2k and 2k + 1. Installed as memory.l2_merge domain_sms = 2 on both devices, evidence experimental (source ldgsts_loaded.<device>.shared_read_domain). Not modelled, recorded: SMs that differ only in bit 16 or bit 32 of their id save a quarter of their shared reads (r 0.74-0.80), and with every SM on one region r reaches 0.28-0.31 where the pair rule gives 0.5; the four-warp cells sit higher (h100 M = 1 0.63-0.64, M = 255 0.50; b300 M = 1 0.51, M = 255 0.42). The rule is applied to every request kind that merges today; for TMA tile loads this rests on the l2_merge v1 cells having grouped consecutive CTAs (neighbouring SMs) and is an assumption until measured with far groups.

addenda.name: issue_cost
addenda.written: before any data of this probe; seen: the per-PC comparison of ten cp.async kernels (fg-line-mem/pc), where hardware charges an LDGSTS 3.5-16 cycles of memory-IO stall in moderately loaded kernels and 41-50 in kernels at the L2 read limit against 2-4.5 simulated, and the unshared stream cells of l2_merge merge_mechanics_rerun (per SM 18.5 / 70.6 / 78.1 bytes per cycle at one / four / eight warps on h100, 19.5 / 75.9 / 124.3 on b300, with one pair of SMs active per GPC)
addenda.text: Question: what issuing a cp.async copy costs the issuing warp, and what it depends on. The engine issues every copy at once and lets the warp wait at the group wait; the kernels above say hardware holds the warp at the copy. Probe ldgsts_issue.cu (run_issue.sh): one CTA per SM, W warps; every warp loops over: clock, C copies back to back (each a warp-wide LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.128 of 512 B from the warp's own part of the CTA's L2-resident region, no shared reads), clock, commit_group, wait_group K, clock. Reported per SM: issue cycles per copy (first to second clock, divided by C), wait cycles per group (second to third), bytes per cycle. Cells, two runs: SM sets t1_m0 (one pair of SMs in every GPC, the rest idle: no GPC limit) and all_m0 (every SM); W in 1 2 4 8; C in 1 2 4 8 16; K in 0 and 3, and K = 1 at C = 4. Copies an SM can have in flight in a cell: F = W x C x (K + 1). Readings fixed here, per device and SM set. a0 = issue cycles per copy at W = 1, C = 1, K = 0. (A) constant issue cost: every cell of t1_m0 is within a factor 1.5 of a0 - then the issue is not where an unloaded SM holds the warp and the missing time is elsewhere. (B) back-pressure: some t1_m0 cells are at or above 2 a0; then the knee is reported in three ways - as the smallest F with issue >= 2 a0 along each of the W, C and K directions - and the form is 'a capacity of in-flight copies per SM' if the three knees agree within one grid step in F, 'per warp' if the knee in C x (K + 1) is the same for every W, otherwise 'mixed' and reported. In saturated cells (issue >= 2 a0) the conservation check issue x C + wait = W x C x 512 / (bytes per cycle of the SM) must hold within 10 percent (it is an identity of the loop if the clocks bracket what they should). all_m0 against t1_m0 at the same (W, C, K): if issue cycles differ by more than 20 percent in cells where the SM rate is GPC-limited (per-SM rate below 0.9 of the t1_m0 cell), the L2 read limit backs up into the issue; otherwise it only lengthens the wait. Prediction: (B), with the issue cost growing once an SM has more copies in flight than it serves in a latency (h100 about 78 bytes per cycle x 420 cycles = 64 copies of 512 B, b300 124 x 360 = 87), and all_m0 backing up into the issue at eight warps. Use: no leaf from this step; the rule (an in-flight capacity of async copies per SM or per warp at which LDGSTS stalls until a copy completes) is designed and replayed after the form is known. The per-SM stream limit is cluster-local; it is asked here because the per-GPC read limit (tma_store_loaded protocol-v5 gpc_scope) decides how long a copy stays in flight.

addenda.name: issue_cost_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-line-mem/issue/{h100,b300}; 88 cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell, runs identical to 0.1 cycle except two cells)
addenda.text: Facts. One pair of SMs per GPC, one warp, nothing waiting: issue cycles per copy 39.0 / 22.5 / 14.8 / 10.6 / 6.5 at C = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 on h100 and 33.0 / 20.5 / 14.0 / 10.1 / 5.2 on b300: each timed interval carries the cost of its clock read (about 30 cycles), so a0 as declared (C = 1) is mostly clock and the factor readings are applied to the per-C baselines instead (change after data); the marginal cost of one more LDGSTS is 6-7 cycles (C = 1 to 8) on both devices. Back-pressure exists (reading B): with eight warps and four groups in flight a copy costs 75-87 cycles on both devices at every C from 2 to 16, with four warps 37-40 at C = 4 and 8; with K = 1, eight warps, C = 4: 71. The first cells above their baseline are those with 64 copies in flight on the SM (W8 C8 K0 30.9 against 10.6, W4 C16 K0 13.0 against 6.5, W4 C4 K3 37.5 against 14.8, W8 C2 K3 75 against 22.5); W = 1 and 2 stay at baseline up to 64 in flight per warp (W1 C16 K3 6.5) except W2 at C = 8 and 16 with K = 3 (15-17). So the knee is in copies in flight on the SM, near 64, not per warp: the declared form 'capacity of in-flight copies per SM'. Every SM active: at K = 0 the issue cost stays at baseline in every cell while the wait grows from 300 to 4000 (h100) / 1700 (b300) cycles - the GPC read limit lengthens the wait; with four groups in flight and eight warps it backs up into the issue (h100 C8 56, C16 225; b300 39, 89), as predicted. Unexplained and blocking any rule: the saturated per-SM rate of this probe is 42.6-42.7 bytes per cycle on both devices (one 512 B LDGSTS per 12.0 cycles) and with every SM active 15.2 (h100) / 35 (b300), about half of what ldgsts_loaded streams with the same instruction, SM sets and warp counts (78.1 / 124.3 and 29.7 / 68.7). Source and destination addresses, byte counts, region size and the SASS of the issue sequence were compared and are the same; what differs is the place of the clock reads (three per round here, one right after the copies) and the walk (each warp its own contiguous part here, interleaved 2 KB chunks there). The conservation check holds (it is an identity). Until the two probes agree, neither the issue capacity nor the per-GPC read limit taken from ldgsts_loaded can be read as a property of LDGSTS alone.

addenda.name: issue_cost_probe_check
addenda.text: Cells (run_issue2.sh; two runs; SM sets t1_m0 and all_m0; W = 4 and 8; C = 4 with four groups in flight): ldgsts_issue with the clock reads in the loop or without them (total time only), and with the walk of each warp contiguous or interleaved as in ldgsts_loaded; C = 16 with and without clocks; ldgsts_loaded itself in the same job. Readings: the factor (clock reads, walk) whose change brings the per-SM rate of ldgsts_issue within 10 percent of ldgsts_loaded in both SM sets is the cause; if the clocks are the cause the issue / wait split of issue_cost is an artefact of timing and the split has to be taken another way (per-PC sampling of the probe); if the walk is the cause the delivery of a cp.async stream depends on where the warps of an SM read (a memory-side fact to be followed); if neither, the difference is elsewhere and is reported. No rule from this step.

addenda.name: issue_cost_probe_check_result
addenda.written: after the data (fg-line-mem/issue2/{h100,b300}; 24 probe cells and 4 reference cells x 2 runs each, no failed cell)
addenda.text: Neither declared factor is the cause. Per-SM bytes per cycle, ldgsts_loaded | ldgsts_issue with clocks, contiguous | without clocks | interleaved | both changed (C = 4, four groups in flight): one pair per GPC, four warps, h100 70.5 | 42.6 | 42.6 | 42.6 | 42.6, b300 75.8 | 42.6 | 42.6 | 42.6 | 42.6; eight warps h100 78.1 | 42.7 (all four), b300 124.3 | 42.6-42.7; every SM, four warps h100 30.0 | 14.9-15.0, b300 63.9 | 35.7-36.1; eight warps h100 29.7 | 14.9-15.5, b300 70.4 | 36.7-37.1. With 16 copies per group and every SM active at four warps ldgsts_issue reaches 33-35 (h100) / 60-63 (b300), i.e. the ldgsts_loaded rate, and at eight warps falls back to 16 / 34. So ldgsts_issue has a ceiling of one 512 B LDGSTS per 12.0 cycles per SM (42.67 bytes per cycle, the same on both devices, with two warps or more) that ldgsts_loaded does not have with the same instruction, byte counts, in-flight groups and SM sets; with one and two warps the probes agree (19 / 37 bytes per cycle). Differences left between the two sources: ldgsts_issue issues, commits and then waits where ldgsts_loaded waits first; its four LDGSTS are back to back in the SASS where ldgsts_loaded has one ALU instruction between them; a 66.5 KB against a 135 KB shared-memory request. Not resolved. Consequences, stated: the back-pressure cells of issue_cost_result (75-87 cycles per copy) are cells at this ceiling and are not evidence of how kernels are held at the issue; the marginal cost of an unblocked LDGSTS (6-7 cycles, against 2-4.5 simulated) and the kernel per-PC numbers stand; the per-GPC read limits installed from ldgsts_loaded stand as measured for that stream form (the replay used the same binary). The question of issue_cost stays open; next: the same probe with the wait before the issue and with the ldgsts_loaded instruction spacing, and per-PC sampling of both probes.

addenda.name: issue_cost_sector_count
addenda.written: after two exploratory ncu runs of both probes (fg-line-mem/issue3, issue4; no leaf from them) and before the rerun declared here
addenda.text: The 'half rate' of ldgsts_issue is a counting error of the probe, not a slower stream: ncu counts exactly 2.000 times the sectors the probe books, in every cell (one LDGSTS of 512 B is delivered and read from L2 as 32 sectors, at C = 1, 4, 16, K = 0 and 3, one to eight warps, both devices), while ldgsts_loaded is at 1.000. In ncu bytes the probe's per-SM ceiling is 84.5-84.9 bytes per cycle on both devices (ldgsts_loaded 78.1 h100, 124.3 b300 at eight warps) and its every-SM cells sit on the per-GPC read limit (h100 30.4 against 29.7, b300 70-74 against 68.7-70.4), so the two probes agree on the GPC limit. The source addresses are the same in both probes; the difference found is the destination: ldgsts_issue has two static shared words before its dynamic array, so its ring starts 16 bytes into a 32-byte unit of shared memory. That a cp.async whose shared destination is not 32-byte aligned is delivered as twice the sectors is the reading this suggests; it is tested by the rerun (ring moved to a 1024-byte boundary): if ncu then counts 1.000, the fact stands for this probe pair and is reported (not installed: the engine has no destination-alignment axis and no kernel is known to depend on it). Rerun: the issue_cost cells unchanged (run_issue.sh) with the aligned ring, readings as in issue_cost with the per-C baselines of issue_cost_result, plus the eight ncu cells of the exploratory run. issue_cost_result and issue_cost_probe_check_result keep their numbers; their per-SM rates are in probe-booked bytes and are to be doubled.

addenda.name: issue_cost_rerun_result
addenda.written: after the rerun with the aligned destination ring (fg-line-mem/issue5/{h100,b300}; 88 cells x 2 runs and 8 ncu cells each, no failed cell)
addenda.text: Sector count: with the ring on a 1024-byte boundary ncu counts 1.000 times the booked sectors in all eight cells on both devices (2.000 before). So a cp.async whose shared destination is not 32-byte aligned is delivered, and read from L2, as twice the sectors - a fact of this probe pair, not installed (no destination-alignment axis in the engine; the kernels with counters do not show a factor two). Issue cost, reading (A) of issue_cost with the per-C baselines: one pair of SMs per GPC, issue cycles per copy at C = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 / 16 with one warp h100 32.0 / 19.0 / 13.8 / 9.5 / 6.1, b300 26.0 / 18.0 / 14.2 / 10.4 / 5.8, and the same within a factor 1.3 with two, four and eight warps and with one, two or four groups in flight, except eight warps, 16 copies, four groups in flight (512 copies on the SM): 29.8 / 28.4. Each interval carries one clock read; between C = 8 and 16 a further LDGSTS adds 1.2-2.7 cycles, between 2 and 8 5-10 (address arithmetic between the copies included). Every SM active: the same baselines in all cells except eight warps, 16 copies, four groups (77.9 / 41.8); the GPC read limit shows in the wait (up to 1975 / 802 cycles per group), not in the issue. So an SM does not hold a warp at the issue of an LDGSTS until several hundred copies are in flight, far more than the kernels of the per-PC comparison hold; the back-pressure cells of issue_cost_result were an effect of the doubled sectors. The prediction (B, knee at 64-87 copies) was wrong. What the kernels show (3.5-16 cycles of memory-IO stall per LDGSTS, 41-50 on two h100 kernels at the read limit, against 2-4.5 simulated) is therefore not reproduced by a contiguous warp-wide copy; those kernels issue predicated, per-lane addressed LDGSTS, which this probe does not have. Not attributed. Also seen: with the every-SM cells both probes sit on the per-GPC read limit (h100 30-31, b300 69-71 bytes per cycle per SM against 29.7 / 68.7-70.4 from ldgsts_loaded), cells with 16 copies and four groups exceed it because a warp re-reads chunks that are still in flight (its own shared reads); and with one pair per GPC this probe streams 123 bytes per cycle per SM on h100 at eight warps where ldgsts_loaded streams 78.1 (b300 121 against 124.3): the h100 figure of 78 is a property of that probe, not a per-SM limit. No leaf and no rule from this protocol step.
